narrative.overview:
Every Game of the Month round is an issue of the club's own 90s game magazine. The GOTM winner is the cover story, the Non-RPG pick is the feature, the club's open business (nominations, the vote) is a highlighter-yellow insert, and every other page is a department: GOTM history is the archive, a member's profile is their bookcase, a game page is its own cover story. The voice is loud and printed: ink-black stock, condensed caps set big, three spot inks that each mean one thing.

Density is magazine density, not dashboard density. A page leads with one monumental object (a round number, a game's two-line headline, a member's name in Anton at banner scale), then settles into ruled departments with labels in tracked condensed caps. Surfaces are hard rectangles with barely-there corners. Depth comes from key art under black legibility scrims, not from glowing cards.

The world refuses the default dark game-tracker: gradient-faded key-art cards, glow accents, gradient text. The app is dark-only (`<html class="dark">`, theme colour #0b0b0d).

The Achievement Hub department: a member's achievements are a binder opened on its gutter, each Achievement Set is a page or two-page spread inside it, and the community hub is a wall of Unlocks under paper-tape day labels. It keeps the ink ground, Anton and Barlow and the 2px paper rules, and adds colour roles (game tint, Rarity inks, Provider colours, foil) used on achievement surfaces only.
keyCharacteristics: Ink-black ground with three spot inks: masthead red for GOTM, violet for NR-GOTM, highlighter yellow for the member's own business.
Anton in caps for every headline and numeral, Barlow Condensed tracked caps for every label, Barlow for reading.
Monumental numerals: the round number, a shelf's count, the days-left clock.
The winner starburst, stamped once, only on winners.
Two-line game headlines, with the second line in the track's accent.
Hard rectangles (2-4px corners) and 2px paper rules under headings.
In the Achievement Hub: game-tint spines, bands and tabs; die-cut icons edged in their Rarity ink; foil stamps only for Platinum, Mastery and Completion.

rules.name: The One Ink Per Track Rule
rules.body: Red means GOTM, violet means NR-GOTM, and nothing decorative borrows either. A GOTM element never wears violet and an NR element never wears red. A game that won both tracks reads as GOTM first.

rules.name: The Yellow Is Yours Rule
rules.body: Highlighter yellow is filled only for calls to action and the GOTM starburst. As type it marks the GOTM headline's second line and interaction states (hover, focus, selection, caret). It never fills a decorative panel.

rules.name: The Red Is Also Here Rule
rules.body: Besides GOTM, masthead red marks where you are: the active sidebar item and the running-head separators. It marks nothing else.

rules.name: The Two-Line Headline Rule
rules.body: A game's title breaks at its subtitle colon ("Metaphor:" / "ReFantazio"). Without a colon it breaks before the last word, and a one-word title is all second line. The second line takes the track's accent: yellow for a GOTM winner, soft violet for an NR-GOTM winner, paper for everything else. Every page that sets a game's name as a headline uses this one rule.

rules.name: The Caps Are the Face Rule
rules.body: Anton and Barlow Condensed are always set in caps through the `font-headline` and `font-label` utilities. Anton never sets mixed case, and it never sets body text.

rules.name: The Empty Track Rule
rules.body: A track with no winner gives its space away rather than apologising for it. On the dashboard, with no NR-GOTM the yellow round panel takes the whole right column at full height and lists the latest nominations. With no GOTM, the NR-GOTM is promoted to the cover in violet, with one small "No Game of the Month this round" note under the numeral. In the GOTM history ledger, where rows must align, an absent track keeps its column as a dashed rule-strong box with a short muted label. Under a title search, that box stays silent, because absence there means "no match".

rules.name: The Multi-Winner Rule
rules.body: Co-winners share one cover, never a carousel. Two winners split it (1.42fr / 1fr). Three put a tall lead panel beside two stacked panels (1.3fr / 1fr). The lead carries the numeral, a paper "N winners" tag and every outbound link, and the narrow panels keep two links. Each winner gets a square letter tile (A, B, C) in its track's ink, and titles step down by panel size. The NR rail does the same: one winner is a feature card, and two or three are a ranked list of covers with A/B/C letters. Side-by-side panels reserve equal blurb height so their stats and actions sit level.

rules.name: The Scrim Not Glow Rule
rules.body: Key art is darkened from where the type sits (from the left for a single cover, from the foot for split panels) with ink gradients (`rgb(11 11 13 / 0.96 to 0.15)`). Art is never faded into a coloured gradient, and nothing glows.

rules.name: The Game Art Is Content Rule
rules.body: A game tint is sampled from the game's own art, so, like key art, it is exempt from the One Ink Per Track Rule: a red or violet tint never means GOTM or NR-GOTM. The system's own tints (the hashed fallbacks) stay off red and violet so a game without art never reads as a track.

rules.name: The Tint Carries Its Type Rule
rules.body: A tint never travels without its contrast colour. Type on a tint is ink or paper, whichever clears AA, and a tint band is always solid, never a gradient.

rules.name: The Foil Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Foil is the system's single sanctioned gradient. It marks only Platinum, Mastery and Completion: the foil stamp, the foil die-cut edge on the Unlock behind one, the Platinum tier dot, the foil frame behind a Platinum on a game's club page, and a Completion signed in the margin. It never sets text, and it never decorates.

rules.name: The Earned Over Total Rule
rules.body: In the Achievement Hub a count reads as an Anton numeral with its total beside it in paper-mute ("23 / 41"). A member's Unlocks are the binder's monumental numeral; slot numbers are two-digit Anton ("07").

rules.name: The Open Binder Rule
rules.body: A member's achievements open as a binder: a rule-coloured cover with 4px corners and a deep object lift holding two ink-2 pages. From xl, a 25rem member page, a 30px gutter of rings, and the index page; filter tabs on the top edge; game-tint tabs past the right edge. Below xl, one page.

rules.name: The Spread Rule
rules.body: A set page is a two-page spread: from xl the view (1.7fr) beside the picked Achievement's details over the Rarity tally (min 20rem), meeting at a shadowed gutter, with game-tint view tabs on the top edge. On phones, one page.

rules.name: The Day Band Rule
rules.body: The hub runs newest first in UTC day bands under paper-tape labels; from xl the Latest wall (62%) sits beside a rail of this week's Highlights (38%). Highlight cards and a day's odd card out span the wall so it never ends on a hole.

rules.name: The Die-Cut Rule
rules.body: Achievement icons are die-cut objects, so they alone round to 6px; the ring frame around a club-page tile follows at 7-8px. Everything else keeps the hard rectangle.

rules.name: The Hand-Placed Rule
rules.body: Objects on the page rest at a tilt, pages stay square: icons at a stable tilt within 1.5deg (straight on hover), foil stamps at -8deg, odds tags at 6deg, day tapes about 1deg alternating, fanned icons by position.

dos: Do colour a thing red only if it is GOTM or "you are here", violet only if it is NR-GOTM, and fill it yellow only if it is a call to action or the GOTM starburst.
Do open every page with one monumental object (a numeral or a two-line Anton headline) and rule every heading with 2px paper.
Do set every game headline with the Two-Line Headline Rule.
Do give an absent track's space to what remains (the yellow panel or the promoted NR cover) on the dashboard.
Do split one cover between co-winners and letter them A, B, C in the track's ink.
Do fall back to the title in Anton on ink-3 when art is missing.

Do keep motion to the single starburst stamp, gentle art scale on hover (1.03-1.04, 500-700ms), the landing marquee and, in the Achievement Hub, an icon straightening from its tilt on hover (200ms), all behind `motion-safe`.
Do keep the Achievement Hub's colour roles (game tint, Rarity inks, Provider colours, foil) on achievement surfaces, and set every tint with its contrast type.
Do keep foil for Platinum, Mastery and Completion.
Do use the glossary in achievement copy: Achievement, Achievement Set, Unlock, Highlight, Rarity, Completion, Mastery, Platinum, Provider, Linked Account.
donts: Don't fade key art into coloured gradients, add glow accents, or use gradient text. Foil is the single sanctioned gradient, and it never sets text.
Don't put a starburst on anything but a GOTM or NR-GOTM winner.
Don't put a breadcrumb inside a page; the running head is the only trail.
Don't add a small tracked-caps kicker or eyebrow above a headline. Track labels sit with a pick's art as data, not above titles as decoration.
Don't use hard offset shadows; shadows here are soft, black and directional.
Don't use emoji or text glyphs as icons; icons are line SVGs (Lucide) at 16-18px.
Don't set Anton in mixed case or at body sizes, or set body copy in Barlow Condensed.
Don't round corners past 4px except avatars, status dots and die-cut achievement icons (6px).
Don't call the GOTM history "Back issues".
Don't put violet or GOTM red on an achievement surface; a game tint that happens to be red or violet is content, not a track.
Don't say sticker, album, pack or pull in the UI. The binder is a visual metaphor; the copy keeps the glossary terms.
